person.note: Mrs Cotton was a friend of Mary Wollstonecraft's . Wollstonecraft stayed with her in Berkshire when she was recovering from her break-up with Imlay. Mrs Cotton visited Wollstonecraft in London when she and Godwin first became intimate. It is unclear whether there was a Mr Cotton, and we cannot be certain that Godwin's entries for 'M Cotton' relate to Mrs Cotton. As a result they have not been coded. Plain 'Cotton' entries after 1797 have not been coded. Ed Pope adds to this: Mrs Cotton 1798 Sonning Land Tax Redemption proprietor and occupier, which suggests she was widowed or separated. Identified in Letters of Mary Wollstonecraft and in Shelley and his Circle only as a friend of Wollstonecraft. I estimate all the entries up to and including 1800 are her whether written Cotton, M Cotton or mrs Cotton and although Cookham is some miles from Sonning. Her letter to Godwin of 18.3.00 (Abinger c5 f95-6) was addressed from Langton Cottage and mentioned Mrs Wilford (see 29.10.1799 above) and Lady Ailesbury as having invited her to stay in London. She was perhaps the Mary Cotton will PCC 1810 of Tyrone Ireland whose will mentioned a former servant to the late Countess of Ailesbury.
